criteria.criterion: Constraint: concurrency must not change band-splitting or backfill decisions; retries (SearchPageFetcher) must still work per band under concurrency; run issues and counters must stay correct.
criteria.plannedImplementation: All band-splitting/backfill decision logic (ShouldSplit, SoldBackfillPlanner.Resolve's Split/Store/None decision, PriceBand.Split) is untouched; only its execution is moved behind worker Tasks with locking around the same merge/enqueue calls. SearchPageFetcher itself is stateless per call (only reads immutable config fields), so its 5-attempt Cloudflare-challenge retry is unaffected by running multiple bands' fetches concurrently. Fetched/BandsPruned/BandsOverCapacityUnsplit/TotalReported/_searchPageFailures are all mutated only inside CollectorRunState.SyncRoot; SoldBackfillPlanner's _dateCache (memoized Task-per-listing under a lock) and _itemPageFetches (Interlocked/Volatile) are now safe for concurrent Resolve() calls from different bands sharing one planner instance.
criteria.plannedVerification: Existing MercariPriceBandCollectorTests Cloudflare-challenge-retry tests (Should_keep_collected_results_and_record_no_search_page_failure_when_challenge_pages_recover_before_success, Should_store_sibling_results_and_record_one_search_page_failed_issue_with_the_challenge_message_when_a_band_is_persistently_a_challenge_page) pass unchanged; the new overlap test's listing-set equality assertion is itself an end-to-end proof that concurrent execution reaches the same band-splitting/merge decisions as sequential execution.
materialConcerns: SoldBackfillPlanner's own internal item-page concurrency (scope item 2: 'the first and last item of a page ... and the margin probe') is only partially implemented. The margin probe (ProbeMargin) is fully parallelized since it unconditionally visits every position in its window regardless of outcome, so concurrency cannot change its result or fetch count. The leading-sample early-exit (IsEntirelyBeforeCutoff) and the single 'oldest'/last-item fetch in Resolve were deliberately left sequential: both currently save fetches via short-circuiting (a locked-in test, SoldBackfillPlannerTests.Should_still_report_none_when_the_first_three_items_all_resolve_before_the_cutoff, asserts an exact fetch count of 3 for that short-circuit), and parallelizing across that boundary would add extra, sometimes-wasted item-page fetches -- a real behavior/budget change the ticket's 'must not change backfill decisions' constraint rules out. SoldBackfillPlanner was made safe for concurrent per-band Resolve() calls (required now that bands run concurrently and share one planner instance) even where its own internal fetches stayed sequential.
criteria.evidence: Named tests pass in the 297/297 Unit run; see materialConcerns for the one deliberately narrower part of scope item 2.
